newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end down after sluggish session.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end down after sluggish session.

text.p: Colombian stocks fell back slightly after a sluggish session in which bank shares provided the only spark of interest.

Bogota's IBB index dropped 0.16 percent to 868.19 on a 2.5 billion peso trading volume -- almost 2 billion pesos of which involved a deal in Banco Industrial Colombiano shares, which sank 3 percent to 3,550 pesos each.
Medellin recorded a thin 257 million peso trading volume, one of the lowest of the year to date. Its IBOMED general price index edged down 0.25 percent to close at 13,632.76.

"The volumes are very low. There's general apathy in the markets because investors are reluctant to put money into shares when they can get a safe return on fixed income," one Bogota broker said. "The Banco Industrial Colombiano deal was a cross trade and the price probably dropped to make it easier for one shareholder to buy off another who was effectively looking for a loan," the broker said.

Other main movers on the Bogota exchange were shares in brewing giant Bavaria, part of the Santo Domingo business empire, which rose 1.47 percent to 3,999 pesos each on total trading worth 167 million pesos.
Banco Ganadero ordinary shares edged down 1.41 percent on a 24.7 million peso volume to 278 pesos, while Bancoquia fell back 1.79 percent to 1,640 on a day's trade of 9.8 million pesos.

In Medellin, Bancoquia shares took a hit, dropping 5.88 percent to 1,600 pesos each on a thin 652,000 peso volume. Cement manufacturer Cementos Argos lost 0.91 percent, ending the day at 5,400 pesos on a total trade of 39.5 million pesos.
